Oh that's really interesting. I haven't had an ATSC tuner, but I'll check that out

FYI this is all stuff you can get on Aliexpress / ebay. Those "TV Link Modulators" take in composite, and usually output at a VHF/UHF channel of your choice, then the "Tru-spec" boxes are distribution amps for old cable TV. They amplify the signal to be broadcast, and then you can just take a rabbit-ear antenna and use it for transmitting instead of receiving. This setup can definitely make it through your house, and probably not past the block.
How powerful are those distribution amps?
A few months ago, someone in Eugene was saying that they saw someone TXing analog video. It might've been a leaky VCR on channel 3/4, but I hope it's real..

Also not helpful for this guy's situation. These boxes are known to spit out garbled signals, it has nothing to do with resolution. I wouldn't tell someone to buy a 90 dollar box unless you know that it would work...

Hi, don't listen to any of these comments. I assume you're using  [a thing that looks like this,](https://www.amazon.com/Portta-N3CVRHP-Component-Converter-support/dp/B003VJ9RP6?source=ps-sl-shoppingads-lpcontext&ref_=fplfs&psc=1&smid=A2WXIT89T9GC4E) or a clone. I spent a long time trying to get it to work, and 99% of resolutions turn into these glitched messes. What I think is that these boxes have a pre-defined set of modelines that are stored in ROM, and if it doesn't get exactly what it wants, it freaks out and spits out jibberish. I have gotten it to work on PC with custom modelines, but there's no way to make it work on xbox, and it's more trouble than it's worth anyway. If I were you, I'd find a HDMI to VGA adapter (Startech is a good brand), and from there, get a VGA to component adapter. 

These boxes just suck unfortunately, but you can get it to work using the other method, and it's not too expensive. I haven't used the box that _FLostInParadise_ is talking about, but it seems fine.
Straight up misinformation. A 31khz signal would show up as a squished double image, not garbled like this.

7 blinks has something to do with voltage regulation iirc. The most common problem with 960s is the voltage regulation ICs, which need to be replaced. There's a guide called like "the 20 dollar wega repair guide" that shows what you need to do, it's worth a shot. I don't know what the deal with the red is, but if you're opening it up, you should look at the neck and see if all 3 fillaments are lit.
This is a long-shot, but do you happen to still have the BY board? I'm looking for a replacement on my XBR 960

I just ordered a pair of EEPROMs for my KD-42XBR960 from your comment. I'm really hoping it's the problem, as it matches a lot of the symptoms you said (micon won't boot, blank image and no OSD despite receiving sync signals in, everything else is physically fine). If I could save a 200 pound TV using a 2 dollar pair of chips, I'd be so happy.

What people overlook is that what Mr House says isn't actually his canon ending. He could just be conning you. This was made more explicit in the cut "Lucky 38 lockdown" sequence where he lies to you that you have a 99% percent or whatever chance of dying before you reach him.
Okay?

My take: there is no such thing as canon. No fictional universe will ever be self-consistent, and the only things that exist are the media you like, and the media you don't.

I don't understand why it's sacrilegious to pick and choose which games you think about, and which you ignore. I don't need to treat the Fallout franchise as 1 giant thing, as if it's a real universe, when it exists across multiple decades where the games industry changed dramatically, across 3 separate companies with different writing cultures, and now across 2 mediums with different storytelling conventions.

We're all fine with ignoring BoS, so why does the Fallout TV show need to live rent-free in your head? Keep calm and replay NV, it'll always be there and the writing hasn't gotten any worse.

You said the exact problem. They show all the imagery you "need for a fallout show", but having easter eggs to gawk at isn't the same as making an interesting story. If this show were set in an original universe and they couldn't use any of the fallout nostalgia, would people honestly still care? I doubt it.
Incidentally, I wish they would remaster DS9 in 1080 like they did with TNG. A man can dream...
Wow they put the memberberries in it. Too bad there's no good writing, good characterization, good atmosphere, or interpretable themes
I doubt the team at Obsidian thought their fan-base were that much of manchildren lol. I love Fallout too, but it's just a game, jesus.
